blocks.text: Endless Possibilities With ChatGPT

Most people who use ChatGPT are only scratching the surface — and don't even know it. They type a question, get an answer, and call it a day. 

It works — but it's a fraction of what the tool can actually do. There's a whole layer of modes and features that completely changes how you interact with it, and this course is where you find out what you've been missing.
Your First ChatGPT Challenge

Imagine you're preparing for a job interview. You need company research, a tailored answer to "tell me about yourself," and three practice questions — all from ChatGPT. Using the same approach for all three would slow you down.

This lesson shows you how to match the right ChatGPT intelligence level and feature to the right task.
Before You Dive In

Open ChatGPT, and the home page offers two modes: Chat and Work. Chat is where everyday tasks happen — questions, drafts, and research. Work is the power mode: an advanced workspace with extra settings for specialized, heavy-duty tasks. This course sticks with Chat: it covers most tasks you'll run into daily. Work gets its own deep dive in a separate course.
ChatGPT runs on a family of models that keep updating. The latest generation, GPT-5.6, comes in three tiers:

• Sol — the flagship and most capable
  • Terra — balances capability, speed, and cost
  • Luna — the fastest and lowest-cost in the family
Tiers and availability may change over time. In a standard ChatGPT conversation, however, you usually choose a reasoning level, not a model.

That reasoning level is the Intelligence setting. It has three levels — Instant, Medium, and High (Pro plans unlock a few more) — and the one you pick shapes how much reasoning ChatGPT puts into your response.

feedbackCorrect.text: When speed matters and the task is straightforward, you want an immediate answer, not extra depth.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Deeper thinking helps with complex work, but for a simple, time-sensitive task like a resume summary, it just adds friction.

options.label: A level built to think longer and go deeper
A level built for speed and immediate output

blocks.text: For quick, straightforward tasks, Instant is your best pick. It's the fastest option, designed for everyday questions and immediate results.

feedbackCorrect.text: Multiple steps and deep analysis = complex task.

feedbackIncorrect.text: This involves multiple steps and research — that's complex.

blocks.question: "Research the company, analyze the role, create interview answers, and give me practice questions"

blocks.text: A multi-step task like this benefits from more reasoning. This is exactly what Medium and High are built for. Both spend more time thinking than Instant, so expect a slower (but deeper) response.
Prefer to skip the choice? Turn on Higher intelligence so Instant scales up to a higher intelligence level when a task needs deeper thinking. Find it in Settings → General.

Think of Intelligence as different gears:
  • Instant — fast responses for everyday tasks
  • Medium — standard reasoning for tasks that need more analysis
  • High — extended reasoning for complex, multi-step work
  • Higher intelligence lets ChatGPT move between Instant and Medium for you
Pick the gear that matches the task, or let auto-switch decide.

blocks.text: ChatGPT's Features

You've just identified which features fit which tasks.

Now, let's understand what each feature does and when to use it.
Feature 1: Web Search

Web Search, as mentioned above, pulls current information from the internet — news, company updates, and recent developments. It's perfect for: company research, current events, and recent product launches.
Let's use the job-hunt scenario: you're preparing for an interview at Nike and need their latest news. Try it.

blocks.exampleResponse:
If you're interested in working at Nike, following the company's latest business developments is a great idea. Here are some of the biggest recent stories: 1. Nike is still in the middle of a major turnaround Recent quarterly results showed:
  • Revenue declined slightly year over year.
  • Sales in Greater China fell sharply (around 17% on a constant-currency basis).
  • The company is investing heavily in new product launches and marketing, particularly around the 2026 World Cup.
This means many teams inside Nike are focused on rebuilding growth rather than maintaining the status quo. 2. Product innovation is back at the center Nike has been emphasizing performance products again after criticism that it relied too heavily on classic lifestyle sneakers. 3. Nike continues expanding global partnerships One recent announcement is that Nike became the official ball supplier for Germany's women's Bundesliga and Supercup, reinforcing its investment in women's football. If you want to work there... These news items suggest Nike is currently looking for people who can contribute to:
  • Product storytelling
  • Sports marketing
  • Brand strategy
  • Digital experiences
Candidates who understand both sports culture and digital consumer behavior are especially valuable as the company works to regain momentum.
blocks.prompt: Ask for web information about Nike's sports clothing division with a Web search.
blocks.template: I want to work [industry]. [Command] Nike's [web information].

blocks.text: Web Search pulled current Nike news directly into the chat — no digging through news sites yourself. For deeper analysis, switch to Deep Research.
Feature 2: Deep Research

Deep Research is built for multi-step, in-depth questions. It can search the web, use uploaded files and connected apps, and produce a structured report with citations. Use it for: market analysis, literature reviews, competitive research, and detailed decision briefs.
Feature 3: Add Photos & Files

The Add Photos & Files feature lets you upload images, PDFs, presentations, text documents, and spreadsheets. ChatGPT can summarize them, compare them, extract information, answer questions about their contents, or analyze their data. Examples: edit an uploaded resume, analyze a spreadsheet, summarize a PDF, or interpret a screenshot.
Feature 4: Create Image

Beyond processing images, ChatGPT can also create and edit images. Describe what you need visually, and ChatGPT generates it. Use this for: portfolio visuals, brand logos, presentation graphics, social media visuals, or just for fun.
OpenAI Platform

In the toolkit, you'll also see OpenAI Platform. It's the developer side of ChatGPT — an API to build your own apps, workflows, and integrations. ChatGPT is the ready-made app you use here; OpenAI Platform is the toolkit for building your own. Below the features menu, you can also search for plugins, files, and skills — like Study and Learn for study plans and quizzes, or others tailored to your work.

ChatGPT's features are tools in a toolkit:
  • Web Search for current info (fast)
  • Deep Research for comprehensive analysis (slow)
  • Files & Photos for analyzing uploads
  • Image Creation for visual content
Pick the tool that matches the job.

blocks.title: Feature Match

blocks.text: Let's combine both: an intelligence level and a feature together. Say you want a quick overview of Nike's corporate culture before an interview. You'd select Instant — the task is straightforward, no deep reasoning needed — and Web search to pull live information.

blocks.exampleResponse:
If you're interviewing at Nike, it's helpful to think of the culture as high-performance, team-oriented, and deeply mission-driven. The company expects people to be competitive, innovative, and obsessed with serving athletes (whether they're professional athletes or everyday consumers).  The five core cultural values According to Nike's careers materials, employees are expected to embody these principles:
  • Serve Athletes: Put customers and athletes first. Decisions should help people perform better and move closer to their goals.
  • Create the Future of Sport: Innovation is everyone's responsibility. Experimentation and calculated risk-taking are encouraged.
  • Be on the Offense Always: Move quickly, stay agile, anticipate change, and act before competitors.
  • Do the Right Thing: Maintain high ethical standards, take ownership, and make responsible decisions.
  • Win as a Team: Collaboration matters more than individual heroics. Success is shared across functions and teams.
What the culture feels like Nike consistently describes its workplace as one where employees are expected to:
  • Think like owners rather than simply execute tasks.
  • Challenge ideas respectfully and ask difficult questions.
  • Move fast and adapt to change.
  • Balance creativity with commercial impact.
  • Be passionate about sport and its positive impact on society.
  • Celebrate team achievements while maintaining high individual standards.
If you're preparing for interviews, expect behavioral questions designed to assess these traits — for example, how you've driven innovation, handled ambiguity, influenced others without authority, or put customer needs first.
blocks.prompt: Ask for a quick overview of Nike's corporate culture with Instant and Web Search.
blocks.template: You are [role]. Give me [output format] of Nike's [topic] and [detail].

blocks.text:
You can now match ChatGPT's intelligence levels and features to different task types and combine them.

This skill multiplies your prompting effectiveness. Knowing how to ask matters, but knowing which tool to use matters just as much.

• Intelligence levels affect speed and reasoning: Instant for everyday tasks, Medium for standard reasoning, and High for more complex work. Some plans include additional levels.
  • Auto-switch handles the choice for you. Let Instant scale up to Medium when tasks need more thought.
  • Features add capabilities beyond text: Web search, Deep research, Add photos & files, Create image, OpenAI Platform.
  • Combine level + feature for the right fit: Like Instant + Web search for a fast company overview.

Deep Research is built for multi-step, in-depth questions. It can search the web, use uploaded files and connected apps, and produce a structured report with citations. Use it for: market analysis, literature reviews, competitive research, and detailed decision briefs.
Feature 3: Add Photos & Files

The Add Photos & Files feature lets you upload images, PDFs, presentations, text documents, and spreadsheets. ChatGPT can summarize them, compare them, extract information, answer questions about their contents, or analyze their data. Examples: edit an uploaded resume, analyze a spreadsheet, summarize a PDF, or interpret a screenshot.
Feature 4: Create Image

Beyond processing images, ChatGPT can also create and edit images. Describe what you need visually, and ChatGPT generates it. Use this for: portfolio visuals, brand logos, presentation graphics, social media visuals, or just for fun.
OpenAI Platform

In the toolkit, you'll also see OpenAI Platform. It's the developer side of ChatGPT — an API to build your own apps, workflows, and integrations. ChatGPT is the ready-made app you use here; OpenAI Platform is the toolkit for building your own. Below the features menu, you can also search for plugins, files, and skills — like Study and Learn for study plans and quizzes, or others tailored to your work.

ChatGPT's features are tools in a toolkit:
  • Web Search for current info (fast)
  • Deep Research for comprehensive analysis (slow)
  • Files & Photos for analyzing uploads
  • Image Creation for visual content
Pick the tool that matches the job.
blocks.title: 💡 Second Discovery

blocks.text: Matching Intelligence and Features to Tasks
Now, let's practice choosing the right intelligence level and feature for different job-search scenarios.

pairs.left: Research a startup's recent funding news
Create a visual diagram for my portfolio
Analyze 10 academic papers on AI ethics
Edit grammar mistakes in my uploaded cover letter

blocks.prompt: Match each task with the most appropriate ChatGPT feature.
blocks.title: Feature Match

blocks.text: Let's combine both: an intelligence level and a feature together. Say you want a quick overview of Nike's corporate culture before an interview. You'd select Instant — the task is straightforward, no deep reasoning needed — and Web search to pull live information.

blocks.exampleResponse:
If you're interviewing at Nike, it's helpful to think of the culture as high-performance, team-oriented, and deeply mission-driven. The company expects people to be competitive, innovative, and obsessed with serving athletes (whether they're professional athletes or everyday consumers).  The five core cultural values According to Nike's careers materials, employees are expected to embody these principles:
  • Serve Athletes: Put customers and athletes first. Decisions should help people perform better and move closer to their goals.
  • Create the Future of Sport: Innovation is everyone's responsibility. Experimentation and calculated risk-taking are encouraged.
  • Be on the Offense Always: Move quickly, stay agile, anticipate change, and act before competitors.
  • Do the Right Thing: Maintain high ethical standards, take ownership, and make responsible decisions.
  • Win as a Team: Collaboration matters more than individual heroics. Success is shared across functions and teams.
What the culture feels like Nike consistently describes its workplace as one where employees are expected to:
  • Think like owners rather than simply execute tasks.
  • Challenge ideas respectfully and ask difficult questions.
  • Move fast and adapt to change.
  • Balance creativity with commercial impact.
  • Be passionate about sport and its positive impact on society.
  • Celebrate team achievements while maintaining high individual standards.
If you're preparing for interviews, expect behavioral questions designed to assess these traits — for example, how you've driven innovation, handled ambiguity, influenced others without authority, or put customer needs first.
blocks.prompt: Ask for a quick overview of Nike's corporate culture with Instant and Web Search.
blocks.template: You are [role]. Give me [output format] of Nike's [topic] and [detail].

blocks.text:
You can now match ChatGPT's intelligence levels and features to different task types and combine them.

This skill multiplies your prompting effectiveness. Knowing how to ask matters, but knowing which tool to use matters just as much.

• Intelligence levels affect speed and reasoning: Instant for everyday tasks, Medium for standard reasoning, and High for more complex work. Some plans include additional levels.
  • Auto-switch handles the choice for you. Let Instant scale up to Medium when tasks need more thought.
  • Features add capabilities beyond text: Web search, Deep research, Add photos & files, Create image, OpenAI Platform.
  • Combine level + feature for the right fit: Like Instant + Web search for a fast company overview.

blocks.text: What's Next?
Next, you'll discover a feature most users walk straight past — Voice Mode: a completely different way to interact with ChatGPT that fits certain tasks better than typing. Stay tuned!
The Voice Mode Opportunity

Imagine you're trying to brainstorm ideas for a new project, but every time you sit down to type, the thoughts won't come. Or you're commuting and have 20 minutes to plan your week — but your hands are full. What if ChatGPT could just listen and chat with you in real life?

That's what Voice Mode does! By the end of this lesson, you'll know when to use it and how to make it part of a real workflow, not just a one-time experiment.
Talking to the AI
You've already learned how to pick the right intelligence level and feature. Now there's one more layer that most people overlook: how to talk to ChatGPT with a Voice Mode.

feedbackCorrect.text: Voice Mode is a fully conversational experience — you speak, ChatGPT responds out loud, and the exchange feels more like a dialogue than a text chat.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Voice Mode isn't transcription or a text-to-speech reader — it turns the interaction into a two-way spoken conversation where both sides communicate through voice.

options.label: It reads your typed messages out loud so you don't have to read the screen
It lets you speak to ChatGPT and hear responses back
It transcribes your voice into text and sends it as a regular prompt

blocks.question: Before we dive in — what do you think Voice Mode actually does?

blocks.text: What Is Voice Mode?

Voice Mode is a two-way spoken conversation with ChatGPT. It's different from Dictation because it doesn't just capture what you say: it listens, responds out loud, follows the thread, and adapts to your tone.

feedbackCorrect.text: Correct! That's Voice Mode working as intended — a real back-and-forth conversation, not a one-shot query.

feedbackIncorrect.text: That's how Voice Mode works. It supports multi-turn conversations, not just transcription.

blocks.instruction: Decide whether this is a real conversation with a Voice Mode

options.label: Voice Mode
Dictation

blocks.question: You tap the microphone icon, say "Help me plan my week," and ChatGPT talks you through a structure

blocks.text: How to Start a Voice Session

In the ChatGPT mobile app, look for the waveform icon in the bottom right corner. On the desktop, the same icon appears in the chat input bar. Once you're in Voice Mode, you'll see a small introduction about Voice.

• Pulsing orb means ChatGPT is listening and is ready to respond.
  • Tap the orb to hide the transcript of your convesration.
  • Tap the X to end the session and return to text.
You don't need to press anything to "send" — just talk. ChatGPT detects when you've stopped and responds naturally.
blocks.title: 💡 What You'll See

blocks.text: Which Voice You'll Get
Depending on your plan, region, and app version, you may see several Voice options:

• Live: the latest experience, built for natural conversation with interruptions, web search, memory, text, and images
  • Advanced: the earlier real-time experience, still used for supported video and screen sharing on mobile
  • Standard: a turn-by-turn experience that transcribes what you say before generating a spoken response
The available options may differ between accounts while Live is rolling out.
When Would You Actually Use It?
Now that you know how it works, here's where it fits in real life:

• "Hey, help me find a good podcast for learning Spanish."
  • "Give me three ideas for a birthday party on a small budget."
  • "Let's brainstorm names for my new project."
You can use it when typing feels inconvenient, or when you want to brainstorm quickly, think out loud, or work through a decision on the go.

• Brainstorming — talking through ideas without editing yourself.
  • Planning — narrating your situation, getting a structured response back.
  • Deciding — saying "Should I do this or that?" and talking it out.
  • Reflecting — using ChatGPT as a thinking partner, not a search engine.
  • Moving — commuting, walking, cooking hands-free.
blocks.title: 💡 Voice Mode Is Best For

blocks.text: You can also customize ChatGPT's voice. ChatGPT gives you several voice options to choose from, with a name and a mood for the voice. Go to Settings → Voice, tap through them to hear each one, and switch any time you want a different feel.

Remember Intelligence levels from the last lesson? Voice has its own. Pick Instant, Medium, or High in the same settings — if those options are available on your account. Use Instant for quick conversation and higher levels for questions that need more reasoning — they may take longer to respond, especially when Voice searches the web.
So, everything you say and everything ChatGPT responds to is automatically saved in the chat. And after your voice session, you can scroll back and read what was covered. Let's try it.

You're in a Voice session, and you ask, "Hey, can you give me three ideas where to go for a summer trip?" Based on what you asked, it answered with three destination suggestions out loud — and you can always follow along in the on-screen transcript if you want to read the response.
Following Up in Voice Mode

ChatGPT may ask a follow-up question to narrow things down, and you simply answer to continue the conversation. For instance, after getting three destination ideas, you could say: "I want to have a more engaging and adventurous type of trip."
When to Switch Back to Text

That's how Voice Mode works in a conversation, but not every task needs to stay in Voice. Writing a document, reviewing a list, or running a calculation are all better handled in text. The good news is you can switch at any point. You can end a Voice session by clicking the X. The full conversation stays in the chat as a transcript — so nothing is lost, and you can continue in text right where you left off.

• ChatGPT follows the thread of the conversation.
  • Each answer builds on the last, just like a real dialogue.
  • When you're done, the full conversation stays as a transcript in the chat.

ChatGPT & Apps

You're planning a trip and ask ChatGPT to find flights, add the best option to your calendar, and create a packing list — all without leaving the chat. Sounds like too much? ChatGPT's Plugins can help with that. By the end of this lesson, you'll know how to connect the apps you already use and let ChatGPT take real actions on your behalf.
ChatGPT Got More Powerful

So far, ChatGPT has been answering your questions, helping you write, and thinking through problems with you. All of that happens inside the chat: it gives you text, and you do the rest. Plugins change that. When you install a plugin, ChatGPT can do things in the real apps: search for flights, make a playlist, or build a design, all from inside the conversation.

Look at the left sidebar: you'll find Plugins there. A plugin can include apps, reusable skills, and app templates. You can browse through apps in categories like Productivity, Creativity, Data & Analysis, Communication, and more, and connect the ones you want.
ChatGPT Alone vs. ChatGPT With a Plugin

blocks.text: What's Next?

You've learned how to pick the right mode and feature, use your voice, and now connect ChatGPT to the apps around you.

Next, you'll discover one of the most visual sides of ChatGPT — image generation: how to describe what you want and bring it to life.
Creating Images With ChatGPT

In this lesson, you'll learn how to use ChatGPT's Image Generation feature to turn your ideas into visuals. You'll discover how to create everything from photorealistic scenes to illustrated designs, edit existing images, and write effective prompts that get you exactly what you need. Let's dive in!
How Image Generation Works in ChatGPT
With ChatGPT, you can create infographics, diagrams, photorealistic scenes, illustrated designs, and more, all within seconds of typing your request.
Where to Find It
To generate an image, you can use one of two ways. The first is to click the "+" icon, select "Create image," and type your prompt.
The second way is to go to the "Images" tab in the left menu, where you can also see templates and all your previous results, stored for quick access.
What makes this feature particularly powerful is how well it understands what you're asking for. It can:

• Render complex scenes with multiple elements
  • Create images with readable text, like signs or menus
  • Generate realistic people with accurate features
And, all of this isn't just for artistic illustration.

With ChatGPT, you can create functional imagery for presentations, marketing materials, educational content, and business documents.

Check it out by trying the following exercises yourself!

blocks.prompt: Let's start by creating a professional image that includes readable text.
blocks.template: Create a [style] storefront sign that says [text] [design style]

blocks.text: See? The text in your image is clear and readable. This is one of ChatGPT's strengths — it can generate images that make text look natural and legible, which is great for signage, product labels, or instructional diagrams.

blocks.prompt: Now, let's create an image of a person doing something specific with their hands.
blocks.template: Create a [style] image of [subject] [action] on a tablet screen

blocks.text: Look at the hands, face, and hair of the woman in the picture: it all looks natural and accurate! ChatGPT handles human features — particularly hands and faces — with precision, making your generated people look realistic. This matters when you're creating professional materials like training content, presentation visuals, or marketing imagery.
Editing What You've Created

Not every generated image is necessarily a final result. You can iterate on it, explore options, and experiment with details and styles. Click Edit on your image to open it in a separate view. There you'll find a Describe edits field for changes and an Aspect ratio control to switch the image's dimensions without regenerating it from scratch.

blocks.prompt: Complete the prompt to edit the businesswoman image from earlier.
blocks.template: [Command] the color of the blouse [new color]

blocks.text: ChatGPT has changed only one element — the blouse. Notice that the content on the tablet screen, facial features, hand positions, and everything else stayed the same. This is the point of editing: you refine visuals without having to start over, which is especially useful when you're fine-tuning materials for clients or presentations.

blocks.prompt: Now push the edit further — transform the entire style of the same image.
blocks.template: [Command] this image [style]

blocks.text: Same scene, pose, and elements — but in a completely different artistic world. ChatGPT can restyle an entire image while preserving its composition. Whether you need photorealism for a business presentation or an illustration for creative projects, you can switch between them without rebuilding the image.

Editing works by describing only what should change:
  • Name a specific element = the rest stays intact
  • Describe a new style = the composition is preserved
  • Switch the aspect ratio = no regeneration needed
One image can carry you from first draft to final asset.
blocks.title: 💡 First Discovery

blocks.text: Putting Precision to the Test
You've created images and reshaped them. Next, let's stress-test the feature with something harder: an image packed with text and specific elements, all of which need to be accurate.

blocks.prompt: Complete the prompt to create a realistic Mac screenshot.
blocks.template: Create a realistic screenshot of [subject] on a Mac, with the note titled [text] and a checklist of [labels]

blocks.text: Check the result: the window chrome, the note title, every checklist item — it all reads correctly. ChatGPT follows detailed, multi-part instructions and keeps text legible across every element you specify. That's what makes it usable for UI mockups, product demos, tutorials, and documentation.

Across every exercise, three creation strengths kept showing up:
  • Text that's actually readable: signs, headers, buttons
  • Realistic human features, including natural hands, faces, and hair
  • Accuracy across multi-part instructions
Combined with iterative editing, this turns generated images into usable assets.
blocks.title: 💡 Second Discovery

blocks.text: Real-World Applications
You've seen what the tool can do; now it's time to apply this knowledge professionally.

For example, teachers, trainers, or instructional designers can generate diagrams, process visuals, or illustrate examples that include accurate labels and text. The clarity makes these images genuinely useful for learning.

blocks.prompt: Imagine you're creating training materials and need a labeled diagram.
blocks.template: [Command] a simple diagram showing the steps of [subject] with clear labels for [elements]

blocks.text:
Also, if you're a business owner or marketer, you can generate logo concepts, product mockups, social media graphics, or presentation visuals.

The ability to include accurate text and realistic details means these aren't just placeholders — they're usable assets.

correctTokens: a white coffee mug on a desk
blocks.prompt: Let's create a product mockup for a business scenario.
blocks.template: Create a [style] image of [product] [specific text element] printed on the side
tokens: a white coffee mug on a desk

blocks.text: Strong Work!

The text on your product mockup is legible and looks professionally placed.

This is precisely the visual you'd use in a pitch deck, marketing proposal, or client presentation.

All in all, you've discovered through practice how the Image Generation feature works — both creating images and reshaping them.

As always, be specific about what you want, mention style when it matters, include any text or details that need to appear, and describe the purpose or context.

• ChatGPT generates images with readable text, realistic human features, and accurate multi-element scenes.
  • You can create both photorealistic and stylized images suitable for business and educational materials.
  • Editing works by describing the change — a single element, a full style, or the aspect ratio — while the rest stays intact.
  • The tool follows detailed instructions precisely, translating your prompts into usable visuals.

blocks.text: What's Next
The following lesson introduces Projects — a feature to create persistent workspaces where ChatGPT remembers context, files, and instructions across multiple conversations. See you there!

blocks.text: What's Next
The following lesson introduces Projects — a feature to create persistent workspaces where ChatGPT remembers context, files, and instructions across multiple conversations. See you there!
What Are Projects & Why Use Them

Are you using ChatGPT by clicking that little "New Chat" button every time? There's actually a smarter way to keep your work organized, especially for longer tasks that include planning! With Projects, instead of dealing with ChatGPT losing track of what you discussed in separate chats, you can keep everything about a task or idea in one spot.
Scenario: Heavy Planning
Let's look at this case: your child's birthday is in three weeks, and you want to use ChatGPT to plan the event. You have:

• A guest list in Excel
  • Venue quotes in your email
  • Theme inspiration screenshots on your phone
  • A dozen text threads with your co-parent about the budget
With so many inputs, you definitely need to develop a multi-step plan.
ChatGPT can help you. But with all the information being scattered, it could be quite difficult.

feedbackCorrect.text: Regular chats work fine, but they don't retain your uploads or context across conversations. For ongoing projects, that means constant repetition.

feedbackIncorrect.text: ChatGPT has conversation memory and handles complex tasks well in any chat. The real issue is that your files and instructions are not preserved across chats.

options.label: ChatGPT can't handle complex tasks in regular chats
You have to re-explain the context and re-upload files every time you start a new chat
Regular chats don't save your conversation history

blocks.question: What do you think is the biggest challenge when using separate ChatGPT chats for multi-step planning?

blocks.text: Your Persistent Workspace

Projects solve this by creating a dedicated space where ChatGPT remembers your progress, stores your files, and follows your specific instructions — across multiple conversations. To start a new project, click "+" next to Projects to create a workspace and give it a name.
One Setting to Check First
Before you hit Create, click the gear icon. It holds one important choice: how your project handles Memory.

• Default: ChatGPT brings what it knows about you into the project and remembers what happens here in your other chats.
  • Project-only: Pick this when the work needs its own space — nothing leaks in, nothing leaks out.
Choose carefully — this setting can't be changed after the project is created.

feedbackCorrect.text: Instructions tell ChatGPT your goals, tone, and constraints for this specific project. Once set, every chat follows these guidelines automatically.

feedbackIncorrect.text: You can chat or upload files right away, but instructions come first because they define how ChatGPT behaves throughout the project — saving you from having to repeat context in every conversation.

options.label: Upload all your files first, and then start chatting
Set instructions for how ChatGPT should respond

blocks.question: Once your first project is created, what do you think is the primary step that you need to take?

blocks.text: Setting Project Instructions
Instructions live in Project settings — a dedicated field where you describe how ChatGPT should respond in every chat within this project. For example, include:

• Tone
  • Constraints
  • Priorities
  • Rules
You can also set instructions by typing them in the prompt field. Let's try it in the following exercise!

blocks.prompt: Complete the prompt to see how you can set instructions for your project.
blocks.template: You are assisting in planning [project] for [occasion]. Keep the budget [budget constraint]. Tone should be [desired tone]. Remember these instructions for next tasks.

blocks.text:
Great! From now on, every chat in this project will follow these guidelines.

That is, ChatGPT will automatically consider age, budget, and tone without having to repeat them.
What's important is that this isn't just about planning birthday parties. The prompt you completed can be used as a template to plan any other project!

Setting instructions transforms your project into a focused workspace. The same principle works for any goal:
  • Project planning: "Keep timelines realistic and highlight risks."
  • Work tasks: "Use professional tone, cite sources."
  • Learning new skills: "Explain like I'm a beginner, use simple examples."
Instructions eliminate repetitive prompting and keep ChatGPT aligned with your needs.
blocks.title: 💡 First Discovery

blocks.text: Uploading Your Party Planning Files

Now comes the powerful part — uploading all your party planning materials to your project. Click Add photos & files — ChatGPT will process and reference everything from guest lists to theme inspirations in any conversation within this project.
For example, imagine you have these files for your party:

• Excel sheet of guests with names, dietary restrictions, and RSVP status
  • PDF document of three venue options with pricing
  • Pinterest screenshots of unicorn theme ideas
Once uploaded, you can use this information in your project without re-uploading it each time.

feedbackCorrect.text: ChatGPT can read, analyze, and reference your files to create plans, extract information, and make recommendations based on your actual materials.

feedbackIncorrect.text: ChatGPT doesn't share files externally or contact vendors. But it can read your uploads and use them to build budgets, timelines, and task lists.

options.label: Create a budget based on venue quotes
Suggest decoration ideas that match your theme inspiration
Share the files with vendors automatically
Count guests and identify dietary restrictions from the Excel file

blocks.text:
To do exactly that, start a chat and prompt ChatGPT to use the data you need.

This is the part when you start working with ChatGPT directly through prompting.

feedbackCorrect.text: Dedicated chats keep your work organized — budget chat stays focused on costs, timeline chat on scheduling. This makes it easy to find past decisions later.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Single threads get messy fast, and random chats create chaos. Strategic chat organization — one purpose per chat — keeps your project navigable and efficient.

options.label: Keep everything in a single chat thread
Start new chats whenever you have questions
Use each chat for one specific purpose

See? You did not need to attach your files again.

Instead, ChatGPT just instantly understood the context and organized specific pricing from the PDF into a complete budget.

Instructions and files function as working memory for your project. Just like you created a budget chat, you can start dedicated chats for:
  • Timeline planning: "Create week-by-week tasks leading to party day".
  • Guest management: "Track RSVPs and dietary restrictions."
  • Shopping lists: "Organize decoration purchases by store."
  • Day-of coordination: "Build a minute-by-minute party day schedule."
Each chat uses the same files and instructions — no repetition needed.
blocks.title: 💡 Second Discovery

feedbackCorrect.text: Projects shine anywhere you need persistent context — trip planning, business development, learning new skills, home renovations, and content creation. The structure is the same: instructions + files + organized chats.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Projects aren't limited to events or anything else. They're designed for situations where context builds over time, and you need ChatGPT to remember files, decisions, and instructions across multiple conversations.

options.label: Yes, Projects work for any multi-step task with ongoing context
No, Projects are specifically designed for a limited number of cases only

blocks.question: So far, we have only covered how to use Projects for planning events. But can this feature be used for other purposes?

blocks.text: Using Projects for Different Purposes

Indeed, this feature can be used for various purposes, including work, hobbies, travel, events, learning, routine planning, and many more.

Let's look at some of these potential applications.
For example, if you're planning a trip to Iceland, you can have a project with chats dedicated to:

• Itinerary building: daily plans with timing and transportation
  • Budget tracking: flight, accommodation, food, activities
  • Reservation management: hotels, restaurants, train passes
  • Packing lists: climate-appropriate clothing and essentials
Upload flight confirmations, hotel bookings, and inspiration images — ChatGPT references them across all planning chats.
Or, if you're developing your business's social media with ChatGPT, you can separate project chats for:

• Content calendar: monthly themes and posting schedule
  • Caption writing: platform-specific posts (Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook)
  • Visual concepts: image generation prompts for graphics
  • Performance analysis: reviewing what content works best
Upload brand guidelines and past successful posts — ChatGPT maintains a consistent voice and style.
Another example: if you're managing a freelance consulting business, your project could include chats for:

• Proposal writing: client-specific service proposals
  • Project tracking: deliverables, deadlines, client communication
  • Invoice generation: monthly billing with hours and expenses
  • Marketing materials: case studies, testimonials, service descriptions
Upload client contracts and past proposals — ChatGPT adapts templates to new opportunities while maintaining professionalism.

The pattern is clear: Projects work best when you have multiple related tasks that share common context — files, goals, tone, and constraints.

Whether planning events, managing work, or learning skills, the structure remains the same: set instructions, upload materials, and organize chats by purpose.

blocks.text: What Are Projects & Why Use Them

Are you using ChatGPT by clicking that little "New Chat" button every time? There's actually a smarter way to keep your work organized, especially for longer tasks that include planning! With Projects, instead of dealing with ChatGPT losing track of what you discussed in separate chats, you can keep everything about a task or idea in one spot.
Scenario: Heavy Planning
Let's look at this case: your child's birthday is in three weeks, and you want to use ChatGPT to plan the event. You have:

• A guest list in Excel
  • Venue quotes in your email
  • Theme inspiration screenshots on your phone
  • A dozen text threads with your co-parent about the budget
With so many inputs, you definitely need to develop a multi-step plan.
ChatGPT can help you. But with all the information being scattered, it could be quite difficult.

feedbackCorrect.text: Regular chats work fine, but they don't retain your uploads or context across conversations. For ongoing projects, that means constant repetition.

feedbackIncorrect.text: ChatGPT has conversation memory and handles complex tasks well in any chat. The real issue is that your files and instructions are not preserved across chats.

Regular chats don't save your conversation history

blocks.question: What do you think is the biggest challenge when using separate ChatGPT chats for multi-step planning?

blocks.text: Your Persistent Workspace

Projects solve this by creating a dedicated space where ChatGPT remembers your progress, stores your files, and follows your specific instructions — across multiple conversations. To start a new project, click "+" next to Projects to create a workspace and give it a name.
One Setting to Check First
Before you hit Create, click the gear icon. It holds one important choice: how your project handles Memory.

• Default: ChatGPT brings what it knows about you into the project and remembers what happens here in your other chats.
  • Project-only: Pick this when the work needs its own space — nothing leaks in, nothing leaks out.
Choose carefully — this setting can't be changed after the project is created.

feedbackCorrect.text: Instructions tell ChatGPT your goals, tone, and constraints for this specific project. Once set, every chat follows these guidelines automatically.

feedbackIncorrect.text: You can chat or upload files right away, but instructions come first because they define how ChatGPT behaves throughout the project — saving you from having to repeat context in every conversation.

options.label: Upload all your files first, and then start chatting

blocks.question: Once your first project is created, what do you think is the primary step that you need to take?

blocks.text: Setting Project Instructions
Instructions live in Project settings — a dedicated field where you describe how ChatGPT should respond in every chat within this project. For example, include:

• Tone
  • Constraints
  • Priorities
  • Rules
You can also set instructions by typing them in the prompt field. Let's try it in the following exercise!

blocks.prompt: Complete the prompt to see how you can set instructions for your project.
blocks.template: You are assisting in planning [project] for [occasion]. Keep the budget [budget constraint]. Tone should be [desired tone]. Remember these instructions for next tasks.

blocks.text:
Great! From now on, every chat in this project will follow these guidelines.

That is, ChatGPT will automatically consider age, budget, and tone without having to repeat them.
What's important is that this isn't just about planning birthday parties. The prompt you completed can be used as a template to plan any other project!

Setting instructions transforms your project into a focused workspace. The same principle works for any goal:
  • Project planning: "Keep timelines realistic and highlight risks."
  • Work tasks: "Use professional tone, cite sources."
  • Learning new skills: "Explain like I'm a beginner, use simple examples."
Instructions eliminate repetitive prompting and keep ChatGPT aligned with your needs.

Now comes the powerful part — uploading all your party planning materials to your project. Click Add photos & files — ChatGPT will process and reference everything from guest lists to theme inspirations in any conversation within this project.
For example, imagine you have these files for your party:

• Excel sheet of guests with names, dietary restrictions, and RSVP status
  • PDF document of three venue options with pricing
  • Pinterest screenshots of unicorn theme ideas
Once uploaded, you can use this information in your project without re-uploading it each time.

Now that you understand Projects, the next lesson introduces Custom GPTs — reusable AI assistants that you build yourself. Ready to customize your AI? Let's go!
The Repetitive Recipe Request

What if you could create your own version of ChatGPT — one that already knows your preferences, follows your rules, and never forgets your instructions?

That's exactly what Custom GPTs let you do. Let's learn how to build one!
The Repetition Problem

Have you ever run out of ideas for what to cook? Or did you get tired of a monotonous diet?

In such a situation, asking ChatGPT for help is a good approach, but it has one issue you might encounter.

blocks.exampleResponse:
Chicken Stir-Fry Ingredients: 2 chicken breasts, sliced 2 cups mixed vegetables (broccoli, carrots, bell peppers) 3 tablespoons of soy sauce 2 cloves garlic, minced 2 tablespoons vegetable oil Salt and pepper to taste Instructions:
  1. Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
  2. Add chicken and cook until golden (about 5-7 minutes).
  3. Add garlic and vegetables, stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
  4. Add soy sauce, season with salt and pepper.
  5. Cook for another 2 minutes until everything is well combined.
Serve hot with rice or noodles!

You might be allergic to certain ingredients, prefer vegetarian options, need calorie counts, or want recipes that always show prep time.

options.label: Because regular ChatGPT cannot personalize responses in any way
To keep meal-planning rules and preferences in one reusable assistant

blocks.question: Why might you create a dedicated GPT for recurring meal planning?

blocks.text: You could keep returning to the same conversation or rely on ChatGPT’s Memory. But for a recurring workflow, it may be more convenient to create a dedicated GPT with its own stable instructions.
For our example of meal planning, that means repeating: your dietary preferences, cooking time constraints, ingredient dislikes, and skill level — in every single chat.
Custom GPTs: Your Reusable Assistant
Custom GPTs solve this by creating specialized assistants that remember your instructions, preferences, and examples — permanently. The coolest thing — you build them yourself!

Instead of adding the same constraints to every prompt, you can say, "Give me a weeknight dinner idea." The GPT applies the dietary preferences, formatting rules, and time limits already included in its instructions.
You might wonder: isn't this what Projects do? Not quite.

• Projects organize files and chats for multi-step work or occasional planning (renovations, events, one-time projects). They're great for storing lots of work-related information in one place.
  • GPTs are for regular, recurring tasks where you repeat the same instructions every time (weekly meal planning, monthly budgets, daily content creation).
Both preserve context, but Projects = occasional big tasks with many files. Custom GPTs = frequent repeated tasks with consistent rules.
Creating Your Cooking Assistant

To start building a Custom GPT, navigate to the left sidebar. Click GPTs → Create. Then, you'll see the GPT Editor with three sections: Create, Configure, and Preview. Note: creating GPTs requires a paid plan and is currently available on the web.

The Create section is where you guide your Custom GPT through prompts. In turn, the Configure section is where you give your GPT name, initial instructions, and upload files. This is where the magic happens.

You can also choose a recommended model and Intelligence level for your GPT. For a cooking assistant, Instant may be enough for quick recipe ideas. If you want a comparison of nutrition plans on top of that, choose Medium or High.

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! Just like with Projects, setting instructions is your first step. Instructions define how your Custom GPT behaves and what it prioritizes.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Just like with Projects, instructions come first. They establish the foundation — role, personality, and constraints — that guide everything your Custom GPT does.

options.label: Setting initial instructions that define the role and behavior
Testing it with different prompts
Uploading files and examples immediately

blocks.question: What do you think is the first step when building a Custom GPT?

blocks.exampleResponse: Perfect! You've established both purpose (cooking help) and personality (friendly, knowledgeable) with clear constraints your Custom GPT will remember forever.
blocks.prompt: Now, complete the prompt to establish the foundation for your Cooking Assistant GPT.
blocks.template: You are [personality] [role] who provides [service] and ingredient suggestions. Keep recipes [complexity level] and always consider [time constraint].

blocks.text: Perfect! You've established the role (cooking assistant), purpose (cooking help), and personality (friendly, knowledgeable) with explicit constraints your Custom GPT will remember forever.

When setting instructions for Custom GPTs, define these core elements:
  • Role: What is this assistant? (cooking helper, writing coach, budget advisor)
  • Purpose: What does it help with? (quick recipes, grammar fixes, expense tracking)
  • Personality: How should it communicate? (friendly, professional, enthusiastic)
  • Constraints: What rules must it follow? (30-minute recipes, formal tone, budget limits)
These elements create a consistent, personalized assistant.
blocks.title: Custom GPT Elements Cheat Sheet

blocks.text: You can set Custom GPTs for any recurring purpose:

• A workout planner that knows your fitness level
  • A writing coach that matches your style
  • A budget tracker that follows your categories
And many more. The pattern is always the same: define role, purpose, personality, and constraints.
Going back to our Cooking Assistant, let's add more instructions to make it work better for you.

feedbackCorrect.text: These details personalize your Custom GPT to your specific needs — making every response immediately useful without adjustments.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Instructions define preferences and rules, not teach techniques. Focus on what makes responses fit your needs: ingredient preferences, dietary restrictions, and formatting rules.

options.label: Detailed cooking techniques for every method
Dietary restrictions or nutritional needs
Specific ingredient preferences and dislikes
Formatting rules like always showing prep time

blocks.question: What additional details could you add to make your Cooking Assistant even more personalized?

blocks.text: Input these details in addition to your initial instructions in the "Create" section. The prompt might look like this:

• User preferences: No cilantro, loves garlic, prefers chicken and fish over red meat
  • Dietary needs: Low-carb options when possible
  • Rule: Always include prep and cook time estimates
These instructions become permanent — your Custom GPT will follow them in every conversation.
Testing Your Custom GPT
With detailed instructions added, let's test the Cooking Assistant with a real request. The "Preview" section will show how it responds.

blocks.exampleResponse:
Quick Lemon Garlic Chicken (25 minutes total) Ingredients: 2 chicken breasts (you mentioned you prefer chicken!) 3 cloves garlic, minced (extra garlic, as you love it) 1 lemon Olive oil, salt, pepper No cilantro (as specified in your preferences) Instructions:
  1. Season chicken with salt and pepper (2 min)
  2. Heat olive oil, sauté garlic until fragrant (1 min)
  3. Add chicken, cook 6-7 minutes per side (14 min)
  4. Squeeze lemon over chicken, cook 2 more minutes (2 min)
Prep: 5 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: 25 min Low-carb and hits your 30-minute target!
blocks.prompt: Ask your Custom GPT for a weeknight dinner idea.
blocks.template: I need [meal type] for [number of people]. I have [time available] and want something [preference].

blocks.text: Notice how your Custom GPT remembered everything: no cilantro, extra garlic, chicken preference, 30-minute limit, low-carb focus, and included prep time — without you repeating any of it. That's the power of Custom GPTs for recurring tasks!
Regular ChatGPT forces you to re-explain context over time. Custom GPTs remember:

• Your preferences and restrictions (dietary needs, ingredient dislikes)
  • Rules you want followed (always show time, keep it simple)
  • Format and structure you prefer (how recipes should look)
  • Constraints that guide every response (30-minute limit, low-carb)

One more control while you're at it: when a plugin — your GPT included — is active in the chat bar, you can set its Thinking effort. Click the chip next to the "+" and pick Standard for everyday requests or Extended for ones that need deeper reasoning, like balancing a full week of meals around your macros.
Beyond Cooking
In this lesson, we used meal planning as an example, but Custom GPTs work for any recurring task that requires repeating the same instructions. For example:

• Monthly budget reviews (same categories, same analysis approach)
  • Weekly newsletter writing (consistent tone, format, audience)
  • Workout planning (same fitness level, equipment, goals)
  • Content brainstorming (same brand voice, audience, topics)
We'll explore these applications in future lessons. For now, just remember: if you're repeating instructions daily, build a Custom GPT.

lessons.title: Build Your Own AI: Custom GPTs

blocks.text: End the Sunday Chaos With ChatGPT

It's Sunday evening. Tomorrow morning, you have your weekly team check-in, and you need to prepare an update.

Your notes are everywhere — chats, emails, phone notes — and you don't know where to start. 45 minutes later, you finally have something usable.

Let's learn a better way!
The Scattered Notes Problem
Every week, you go through the same routine of manually organizing everything into a coherent structure for the meeting.
Let's do the math:

• 45 minutes every Sunday
  • 52 weeks per year
  • 39 hours annually on one task
And all of this on a weekend day!

feedbackCorrect.text: The information exists — it's just fragmented. Collecting and organizing it is where time disappears.

feedbackIncorrect.text: What to say becomes clear once information is organized. The real bottleneck is gathering scattered notes and creating structure — that's what eats up 45 minutes every week.

options.label: Gathering scattered information from multiple sources into one structure
Thinking about what and how to say during meetings

blocks.question: What do you think is the biggest challenge when preparing for recurring meetings?

blocks.text: With ChatGPT, you can turn messy notes into a structured agenda in 5 minutes!
Discovering Prompting Techniques

Sequential task chaining breaks complex workflows into linked steps, with each step building on the previous output. Therefore, instead of "do everything at once," you guide ChatGPT through a logical sequence.

Now let's build this chain together — step by step. You'll discover each step by figuring out what makes sense next.

Ready? Let's start with your scattered update notes.
Here's what you have scattered across apps:

• Chats: "Finished the client presentation deck yesterday."
  • Email: "Next week: need to finalize budget proposal and schedule Q2 review."
  • Phone note: "Ideas for improving onboarding process — ask team for input."
  • Another Slack: "Meeting with Sarah went well, she approved the timeline extension."
  • Random note: "Follow up with vendor about delayed shipment."
This is the raw material you're working with.

feedbackCorrect.text: Smart! Before you can organize, you need clarity. Cleaning up the raw notes into a readable format is always Step 1.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Complete sentences add unnecessary detail at this stage. And grouping works better after cleanup. Step 1 is always about getting clarity first — brief, scannable summaries.

options.label: Group everything by category right away
Rewrite everything in complete sentences with full context
Turn each note into a clean, single-line summary

blocks.question: Looking at these scattered notes, what should be your first step?

blocks.exampleResponse:
Weekly Notes Summary:
  • Completed client presentation deck
  • Next week priorities: finalize budget proposal, schedule Q2 review
  • Idea: improve onboarding process, need team input
  • Sarah approved the timeline extension in the meeting
  • Need to follow up with the vendor on the delayed shipment
blocks.prompt: Now, complete the prompt to see how messy notes can be transformed into clean summaries.
blocks.template: Here are my weekly notes: *notes pasted*. [Command] each note [format].

blocks.text:
See what just happened? You took scattered, messy notes and turned them into a clean, scannable list in seconds.

That's the power of Step 1. It creates a clear foundation that you can build on.

feedbackCorrect.text: Now that everything is readable, grouping by category will reveal patterns and make your update structured.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Adding details or writing the introduction comes later. Right now, organizing summaries into categories helps you see the big picture first.

options.label: Expand each summary with more details and context
Start writing the introduction for your team update
Group related items into categories like "Completed," "Next Week," and "Follow-up"

blocks.question: Now that you have clean summaries, what should be your next step?

blocks.exampleResponse:
Weekly Update — Organized: Completed This Week:
  • Client presentation deck finished
  • Sarah approved the timeline extension
Next Week Priorities:
  • Finalize budget proposal
  • Schedule Q2 review
In Progress:
  • Onboarding process improvements (need team input)
Follow-up Needed:
  • Vendor delayed shipment issue
blocks.prompt: Complete the prompt to ask ChatGPT to organize your clean summaries into logical groups.
blocks.template: Based on the summaries above, [command] [group count] and [labeling instruction] to each category

blocks.text:
Now you can see exactly what was accomplished, what's coming, and what needs attention.

This is where the "chain" gets powerful. Each step builds on the last, making everything clearer and more actionable.

feedbackCorrect.text: Now that everything is organized, you can create the professional update — what happened, what's next, and what needs support.

feedbackIncorrect.text: You don't need more categories or paragraphs. The final step is turning your organized information into a clear, actionable update.

options.label: Rewrite everything in paragraph form
Add more categories to make it more detailed
Turn categories into a polished team update with context and next steps

blocks.question: With your notes organized into categories, what should the final step be?

blocks.exampleResponse:
Weekly Team Update — Week of Dec 9 This Week's Wins: ✅ Completed client presentation deck (ready for Thursday pitch) ✅ Secured timeline extension approval from Sarah (new deadline: Dec 20) Next Week Focus:
  • Finalize budget proposal (deadline: Wednesday)
  • Schedule Q2 review meeting (coordinate with finance team)
  • Launch onboarding improvements (gathering team input this week)
Needs Attention:
  • Vendor shipment delay — following up on Monday to resolve before the client deadline
How You Can Help: If anyone has feedback on onboarding improvements, please share by Tuesday!
blocks.prompt: Transform your organized categories into a complete weekly update.
blocks.template: Using the categories above, create [document type] that includes [accomplishments], [upcoming work], and [support needed]

blocks.text: Look at that! You went from scattered messages and random notes to a polished, professional update:

• Accomplishments highlighted
  • Priorities clear
  • Support needs identified
This is sequential task chaining in action. Each step made the next one easier and more precise.

Sequential task chaining works by breaking complexity into manageable steps:
  • Clarify first: transform messy inputs into a clean, readable format
  • Structure second: group related items to reveal patterns
  • Execute third: create the final output with all details
Each step validates before moving forward. This prevents overwhelm and ensures consistent quality — no matter how scattered your starting point is.
blocks.title: 💡 Technique Unlocked

blocks.text: Beyond Weekly Updates
In fact, this technique works for any situation where you need to gather, organize, and structure scattered information.
Some examples where you can apply sequential prompting:

• Planning a home renovation: Contractor quotes, measurements, design ideas → Clean summaries → Group by room → Create timeline and budget
  • Weekend trip planning: Notes about hotels, activities, restaurants → Clean list → Group by day → Create itinerary
  • Work project kickoff: Emails, meeting notes, requirements → Summarize each → Categorize by theme → Build project plan
These are different applications of the same principle.

blocks.title: Complete Sequential Chain

blocks.text: Great Job!

Now you know how to turn 45 minutes of scattered-note chaos into 5 minutes of structured work. Sequential task chaining isn't just a technique — it's a reusable system you can apply every week with different inputs. Same process, consistent results.

• Sequential chaining breaks complex tasks into linked steps, with each step building on the previous output.
  • Step 1 always creates clarity (clean up the mess).
  • Step 2 reveals structure (group and categorize).
  • Step 3 makes it actionable (create the final output).
Save this pattern and reuse it with different inputs!

blocks.text: What's Next?

Next, you'll learn how to rewrite any message for tone and clarity and match your personal voice using examples with ChatGPT. 

Let's keep going!
The Difficult Message Problem

We all have messages we keep putting off — the team update nobody wants to deliver, the "no" to a friend's favor, or the awkward email to a landlord. Whatever the situation, finding the right tone is hard.

Let's learn how ChatGPT can help you get it right.
The Tone Challenge

Here are the first drafts for each situation: Work: Subject: Project Timeline Change "Team — due to budget constraints, we're pushing the feature launch back 6 weeks. I know this isn't ideal, but we need to adjust. The new target date is May 15. Let me know if you have questions."
Personal: "Hey — I can't help you move this weekend. I have other plans. Good luck with it."
Every day: "Hi, the heating still isn't working. This is the third time I'm asking. Please fix it."

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! The information is clear in all three, but the tone feels dismissive. No acknowledgment of impact, no empathy, just facts and directives.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Length and detail aren't the main issues. The problem is tone — all three read as cold and transactional when the situation calls for something more human.

options.label: They're too short and don't provide enough detail
They don't include a clear action plan
The tone is too blunt and doesn't acknowledge the other person's feelings or situation

blocks.question: What's the biggest problem with all three drafts?

blocks.text:
This is where many difficult messages fail: the content is fine, but the tone is wrong.

However, ChatGPT can help you rewrite for the right tone while keeping your message clear!
Basic Tone Adjustment

First, let's ask ChatGPT to rewrite your work email draft with a more empathetic, professional tone. Subject: Project Timeline Change "Team — due to budget constraints, we're pushing the feature launch back 6 weeks. I know this isn't ideal, but we need to adjust. The new target date is May 15. Let me know if you have questions."

blocks.exampleResponse: Subject: Important Update on Feature Launch Timeline Dear Team, I want to share an important update regarding our feature launch. Due to organizational budget adjustments, we need to extend our timeline by six weeks, moving our target launch to May 15. I recognize this news is disappointing, especially given the significant effort and progress you've all made over the past three months. Your dedication to this project has been exceptional, and this change doesn't reflect the quality of your work in any way. While this adjustment is necessary from a budget perspective, I want to ensure we use this additional time strategically. Let's schedule a team meeting this week to discuss how we can optimize our approach and maintain momentum. I'm available if anyone would like to discuss this change or has concerns about how it affects their work. Thank you for your continued commitment and flexibility. Best regards, [Your Name]
blocks.prompt: Ask ChatGPT to adjust the tone of your email.
blocks.template: [Command] this email to be [tone quality] while staying clear and direct: *your pasted draft*

feedbackCorrect.text: ChatGPT improved the tone and added empathy, but now it sounds like a corporate template. It lost your personal voice — the way YOU actually communicate with your team.

feedbackIncorrect.text: The tone improved, but there's a new problem: it doesn't sound like you. Generic professional language can feel impersonal. You want ChatGPT to improve your writing without erasing your voice.

options.label: Yes, this is perfect and ready to send because it feels personal
Better tone, but it sounds too formal and generic
No, it's actually worse because it's too long now

blocks.question: Is this rewritten version better than the original draft?

blocks.text: This is a common issue when using AI to rewrite: it improves one thing (tone) but loses something important (your voice). The solution? Show ChatGPT examples of how you write, then have it match your style while improving clarity. Now let's try matching style through this personal scenario: "Hey — I can't help you move this weekend. I have other plans. Good luck with it."
Style Matching With Examples
ChatGPT can match your writing style if you give it examples to learn from:

• Example 1: "Hey, just saw your message — sorry for the slow reply! Would love to help, but my weekend is completely gone with family stuff. Can we figure out another way I can help you out?"
  • Example 2: "Ugh, I feel terrible about this, but I genuinely can't make Saturday work — already committed to something I can't move. Let's catch up properly next week though, I miss you!"
  • Example 3: "So sorry, I'm the worst — completely forgot to reply. I can't do this weekend, but I'm free the one after if that helps at all?"

blocks.exampleResponse: Hey — I'm really sorry, I can't help with the move this weekend, I already have plans I can't shift. I feel bad missing it, but I hope it all goes smoothly! Let me know if there's another way I can help or if you want to catch up after 💛
blocks.prompt: Complete the prompt to see how shared examples of your typical writing style can affect the result.
blocks.template: Here are examples of how I write to close friends: *pasted examples*. Now, rewrite this message to be [tone], while staying [quality requirement].

blocks.text: See the difference? Now it sounds like you:

• Conversational ("won't be welcome news," "I'm around if anyone wants to talk")
  • Direct without being cold ("this is frustrating")
  • Empathetic but not overly apologetic ("budget reality")
  • Maintains your casual style ("rolling with this")
ChatGPT matched your voice while improving the structure and clarity.

Examples teach ChatGPT your voice:
  • Without examples → Generic professional language
  • With examples → Your natural style, but polished
Providing 2-3 samples of your style preserves your authentic voice while improving clarity and tone.
blocks.title: 💡 First Discovery

blocks.text: Iterative Phrase Refinement
Same pattern — your voice, your warmth, the message still lands. Now, let's take it one step further with an everyday situation.
Phrase Refinement — Everyday

Your heating has been broken for weeks, and your landlord keeps ignoring you. Your draft is frustrated and blunt: "Hi, the heating still isn't working. This is the third time I'm asking. Please fix it."

feedbackCorrect.text: Keep the conversation going. ChatGPT has context from the previous version and can adjust specific parts without redoing everything.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Starting over wastes the work you've already done, and manual editing loses ChatGPT's help. Iterative refinement through conversation is more efficient — just point to what needs changing.

options.label: Ask ChatGPT to refine just that phrase while keeping everything else
Rewrite the entire email from scratch with a new prompt
Manually edit that phrase yourself without using ChatGPT

blocks.question: What do you think you should do when one specific phrase needs adjustment?

blocks.exampleResponse: Here's a more professional, firm version that keeps urgency clear: Your draft: Hi, the heating is still not working. This is now the third time I've reported the issue. Given the ongoing problem, I need this to be resolved as a matter of urgency. Please confirm when this will be fixed. More direct version of your phrase: Please provide a clear update on the repair timeline and expected resolution date.
blocks.prompt: Ask ChatGPT to rewrite your landlord message with the right tone, then refine one phrase that still feels off.
blocks.template: Rewrite this message to be [tone quality] while making it clear this needs to be [urgency]: *your draft*. Then make this phrase [change request]: "I'd appreciate an update."

blocks.text:
Firm, clear, professional — and much more likely to get a response. Once you're happy with the message, you're ready to send it.

But if your message is longer — say, a formal complaint — that's when it's worth opening Canvas for a final polish before hitting send.

Canvas is ChatGPT's side-by-side editor — it opens a separate panel next to the chat where you can refine your draft with targeted edits without rewriting everything from scratch. ChatGPT opens Canvas on its own when it sees the task calls for one — typically for writing or code longer than 10 lines. If you want to be sure it opens, add "use Canvas" to your prompt.

Let's say you asked, "Write a formal complaint about my heating issue based on the message I just wrote." ChatGPT recognizes this as a drafting task and opens the draft in Canvas, ready for refinement. From there, edit by describing what you want in the Ask for changes bar.

You just used the style-guided rewriting approach. Here's how:
  1. Start with your draft, even if the tone is wrong.
  2. Ask for specific tone adjustment: "more empathetic and professional."
  3. Provide examples of your style: 2-3 past emails showing your voice.
  4. Have ChatGPT rewrite in your style while improving clarity.
  5. Refine specific phrases iteratively through conversation.
This preserves your authentic voice while polishing difficult messages.
blocks.title: 💡 Second Discovery

blocks.text: This approach works for any difficult communication you need to write:

• Saying no to a request: Your draft sounds too harsh → Rewrite in your style with an empathetic but firm tone
  • Giving constructive feedback: Your draft is too soft → Rewrite with a direct but supportive tone
  • Announcing a deadline change: Your draft is too apologetic → Rewrite acknowledging impact while staying clear
  • Declining a meeting: Your draft sounds dismissive → Rewrite showing respect for their time while protecting yours
Same pattern: draft → tone adjustment → style matching → phrase refinement.

feedbackCorrect.text: Without examples, ChatGPT defaults to generic professional language that won't sound like you. Examples teach it to your voice — your phrases, your level of formality, your personality.

feedbackIncorrect.text: "Professional tone" produces corporate templates. Examples are what preserve your authentic voice, while ChatGPT improves structure and clarity. Skip them, and your writing won't sound like you anymore.

No, examples are essential

blocks.text: The Difficult Message Problem

We all have messages we keep putting off — the team update nobody wants to deliver, the "no" to a friend's favor, or the awkward email to a landlord. Whatever the situation, finding the right tone is hard.

Let's learn how ChatGPT can help you get it right.
The Tone Challenge

Here are the first drafts for each situation: Work: Subject: Project Timeline Change "Team — due to budget constraints, we're pushing the feature launch back 6 weeks. I know this isn't ideal, but we need to adjust. The new target date is May 15. Let me know if you have questions."
Personal: "Hey — I can't help you move this weekend. I have other plans. Good luck with it."
Every day: "Hi, the heating still isn't working. This is the third time I'm asking. Please fix it."

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! The information is clear in all three, but the tone feels dismissive. No acknowledgment of impact, no empathy, just facts and directives.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Length and detail aren't the main issues. The problem is tone — all three read as cold and transactional when the situation calls for something more human.

They don't include a clear action plan
